message.text: `VerificationRecord.refusal` now keeps whichever equal-verdict report came first. That includes a lowered one, even when a later report at the same verdict holds the claim at the lens's severity. The base decision and design say the reverse, in words: on equal verdicts the record keeps the higher severity, and two `confirmed` reports that disagree on a lowering leave the finding unlowered, in either order. The change also edits the decision record to match (the new 2026-11-28 decision amends the re-scope decision's "conflicting reports" section, and docs/design.md line 172 is rewritten). Under this lens's rules that edit does not excuse the change: it is judged against the base text, because it weakens a fail-closed rule about a model moving a finding out of the blocking set.

evidence.snippet:
## What survives: conflicting reports

The grain is the claim. Each lens sighting is one claim, and a lowering belongs to the stored record for its claim.

- The strongest verdict still wins: `confirmed` over `plausible` over `refuted`, as [conflicting verifier reports](2026-10-06-verifier-conflicting-reports.md) set it. A weaker report leaves the record unchanged.
- On equal verdicts for one claim, the record keeps the higher severity. A later equal report never weakens a stored one. So two `confirmed` reports that disagree on a lowering leave the finding unlowered, in either order.
- When an equal report replaces a stored one, the record keeps the winning report's reason and evidence.
- The merged defect takes the highest severity among its claims after lowering. A claim no verifier judged keeps its own severity.

The verifier has one chance per claim, by design, so that a second call can never be used to lower: a report whose lowering the fence refused is stored unlowered, and a later equal report does not correct it. So that the one chance is a fair one, the label line Melian writes for each claim, outside the boundary, names the severity the lens reported.

Reports are judged per claim. The strongest verdict still wins. On equal verdicts for one claim, the record keeps the higher severity, and a later equal report never weakens a stored one. The merged defect takes the highest severity among its claims after lowering.

1. `report_verdict` refuses a second report of a claim unless its verdict is stronger than the stored one. A replay of the stored report is taken. Otherwise the first report stands whole: its reason, its evidence, its sameness answers and its lowering. A stronger later verdict still replaces the first report whole, its lowering included, as before. The refusal says which verdict is stored and any lowering it holds.
2. `report_verdict` refuses a lowering with no evidence location at the head before anything is stored, and says that nothing was recorded, so the verifier can send the report again with evidence, or without the lowering.

The old rule is replaced. Under it, a later report at an equal verdict replaced the stored one whole when it was unlowered, so it could undo a lowering and overwrite the reason. It was written for a second judgement of the claim, and it was being met by placeholders.

explanation.whatToDo: Keep the first report's reason against placeholders, but let a later equal report that removes the lowering win. That restores the base's higher-severity rule. One way: in `refusal`, accept an equal-verdict report with no `lowered` when the stored report has one. Then add a test where a confirmed lowered report is followed by a confirmed unlowered one and the claim ends unlowered.
explanation.whyHere: Under the base rule, when the verifier disagreed with itself about a lowering, the claim kept the higher severity. The verifier could always hold a finding at the lens's severity with a later equal report. Now a lowering made by a `confirmed` first report cannot be withdrawn. No verdict is stronger than `confirmed`, so every later report is refused, and the claim stays one step down even though the verifier's latest judgement says it should not be. The head decision's "What this gives up" names only the lost chance to correct a reason. It does not name the lost chance to withdraw a lowering.

properties.failureScenario: A design-lens P1 claim c1 goes to the verifier. The verifier calls `report_verdict` with `{verdict: "confirmed", evidence: [head location], lower: {severity: "P2", reason: "only caller validates"}}`. The fence accepts the lowering, and `upsertVerification` stores the report with `lowered: {from: P1, to: P2}`. The verifier then reads a second caller that does not validate. It sends `{verdict: "confirmed", reason: "A second caller passes unvalidated input; P1 stands"}` with no `lower`. In `refusal`, the two reports serialise differently (line 131), and `confirmed` is not stronger than `confirmed` (line 132). So it returns the refusal string, and `upsertVerification` throws (findings.ts 1069-1070). The stored lowered report stands, and the finding resolves at P2. Under a table where P1 blocks and P2 is advisory, the review passes without the acknowledgement it needed. Under base, `#stronger` returned the unlowered report on equal verdicts, so the claim stayed at P1. The verifier has no way to undo this, because it cannot send a verdict stronger than `confirmed`.
